title: Regional fanout-induced SLO miss; quarantine timeline and action plan
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: A sustained traffic surge amplified by region-affinity fanout and a mis-tuned circuit hysteresis caused a cascade of degraded tail latency and an SLO miss for /v1/generate across EU and NA. This document records the timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and a prioritized action plan to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-17T09:42Z detection: Alerts for p99 generation latency in eu-west began. 09:47 increased cross-region fanout observed when primary qps hit spike. 09:52 first circuit breaker triggered in eu-west; stale circuit hysteresis kept region in degraded state though healthy tokens were available. 10:05 kv-cache warmup lag: cold shards were rehydrated slowly due to serial prefetch; downstream region received extra load. 10:22 failover quarantine activated but sticky-affinity caused uneven distribution. 10:45 rolling traffic rebalancing and staged circuit resets restored normal p99 by 12:10.
impact: ~55 minutes of elevated p99 across 2 regions, 6% of client requests experienced >2x latency, SLO (p99 < 200ms) breached for the hourly window. No data loss; some paid customers saw degraded UX and filed support tickets. Estimated customer-facing error budget burn: 0.9%.
root_cause: Three factors combined: (1) an unexpected microburst pattern from a third-party integration produced correlated token-heavy requests; (2) circuit-breaker hysteresis thresholds were too coarse relative to the new microburst shape, preventing fast recovery and amplifying failover; (3) KV cache prefetching used a serial warmup path, which caused slow shard rehydration and uneven load transfer between regions.
detection_and_alerting_findings: Existing SLO alerts fired (p99 latency) but did not surface the root of fanout-affinity coupling. We lacked a composite alert that correlates circuit state changes + kv-cache warmup rate + fanout ratio. The alert noise made operator triage slower. Playbook steps were present but missing the specific runbook for circuit hysteresis resets.
immediate_mitigation: We performed coordinated soft resets of impacted circuit breakers with staged cooldowns (10m, 5m) to avoid a second surge. Adjusted routing to shift 20% of new load to an underutilized secondary pool while warming KV caches aggressively (parallel prefetch). Rate-limiting applied temporarily at ingress for the offending upstream client to smooth bursts.
permanent_fix_plan: 1) Implement faster circuit hysteresis with adaptive backoff based on recent qps variance (runtime-1.22). 2) Parallelize KV shard prefetch with bounded concurrency and priority for hot prefixes. 3) Add a composite alert that correlates circuit state changes + kv prefetch rate + cross-region fanout ratio. 4) Create a failover quorum policy to avoid sticky-affinity transfers during asymmetric capacity loss. 5) Update canary and chaos tests to include microburst-shaped load profiles.

qa_and_validation: Merged feature branches will be validated against synthetic microburst load (sustained 20k rps with 10-50ms bursts) in staging. End-to-end tests will assert p99s remain under 200ms with the adaptive hysteresis enabled. KV prefetch metrics must show >4x warmup rate vs serial baseline.
decision_tradeoffs: Adaptive hysteresis involves more complex state and potential oscillation risk; we chose a bounded damping factor and a secondary watchdog to reset hysteresis if oscillation detected. Parallel prefetch increases memory pressure — we bound concurrency by region and shard to cap worst-case memory increase.

communication_and_customer_notes: We published an incident summary to customers with affected SLAs and offered a dedicated review for top 10 customers. CS followed up with the 5 impacted customers who reported degraded UX. Internal notification sent to on-call and platform engineers at 10:20Z; postmortem published to engineering and signaled in weekly ops review.
current_status_and_next_steps: Primary mitigations completed and verified. ENG owners assigned for permanent work. Expect release of runtime-1.22 with adaptive hysteresis and kv prefetch improvements in April canary window. Tracking follow-up tickets in the resilience-fallback project; next sync scheduled 2026-03-04.
